title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.

providers.name: Box
providers.scope_notes: Do not substitute Box Shield location/anomaly detection or corporate firewall allowlisting for API source-IP enforcement.

controls.name: Admin authorization of server authentication apps
controls.what: JWT, CCG and Limited Access (App Token) apps cannot be used in the enterprise until an admin authorizes them by Client ID.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps > Server Authentication Apps
controls.quote: authorize and enable custom server authentication apps, such as JSON Web Token (JWT) apps, client credential apps, and limited access apps,

controls.name: Re-authorization on scope/access changes
controls.what: Authorization is a snapshot; changed scopes or access level need admin re-authorization.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps > … > Reauthorize
controls.quote: The authorization is a snapshot in time. This means that if a developer revisits the Developer Console and changes the configuration, the Admin must re-authorize the application in order for generated Access Tokens to reflect the changes.

controls.name: Disable unpublished platform apps by default
controls.what: Unpublished custom apps (OAuth and server-auth) are disabled until an admin enables them.
controls.setting: Admin Console > Enterprise Settings > Platform Apps
controls.quote: When you select Disable unpublished platform apps by default, Box disables all unpublished platform apps by default.

controls_unknown: No admin setting found that blocks developers from generating developer tokens; tokens expire after 60 minutes and inherit the app's scopes and the user's access.
Whether Box offers API source-IP enforcement for app tokens (no admin doc found; Shield/firewall not counted).
Whether new Limited Access (App Token) apps can still be created.
Whether Box SSO requirements constrain OAuth token issuance for managed users (not checked).
Whether app access level (App only vs App + Enterprise) and scopes can be overridden by the admin at authorization time; docs show them set by the developer in the Developer Console.

authentication.summary: Fixed bearer token generated in the Developer Console for a Limited Access App. It acts as the app's service account and is mainly intended for Box View previews.

federation.details: Manually generated static token; no external identity exchange is documented. The token can be the subject token for Box downscoping.

ip_restriction.boundary: A Box staff community answer describes an enterprise IP allowlist that narrows both web app and API access, with no per-app option. Current official documentation of its coverage for App Token calls was not found; confirm with Box.

lifetime.summary: Set per token: auto-expire or never expire

renewal.summary: The token is reused until it expires or is revoked; replace it by generating the secondary token, switching over, then revoking the primary.

administration.summary: Developer creates a Platform App; an enterprise admin must authorize it in the Admin Console before tokens can be generated. Two tokens (primary and secondary) may be active and each can be revoked in the console.
administration.conditions: Box calls these legacy Limited Access Apps and says the approach is being replaced by CCG and JWT, which support all App Token endpoints plus 150 more. Whether new App Token apps can still be created is not stated.

sso.details: App Tokens are server-side authentication, which Box says does not use SSO.

offboard.details: App Tokens are restricted to the application's Service Account.

inventory.details: Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps > Server Authentication Apps lists apps with authorization/enablement status, not individual keys or tokens.

expiry.ui: Developer Console > (app) > Configuration > Primary Access Token > Generate Key; choose auto-expire or never

reads.ui: Admin Console > Reports > Create Report > User Activity; filter Action types to Downloaded

token_format.notes: Fixed, long-lived Primary/Secondary App Token; may be set to expire or never expire. No documented prefix; no GitHub secret scanning pattern.

log_sources.name: Box Enterprise Events (GET /events, stream_type=admin_logs / admin_logs_streaming)
log_sources.notes: Admin/co-admin with reporting permission. admin_logs: 1 year history; admin_logs_streaming: ~2 weeks live. Admin Console reports: 7 years.

credential_id_fields.notes: User mini object (id, name, login) acting; id 2 = Unknown User
User session; not populated on all events
Event-specific details ('how a user performed an event'); per-event keys not fully documented

lifecycle_events.notes: Programmatic access by a Box application

anomaly_cues: App service account doing anything other than upload/preview (e.g. collaborations, shared links)
Use from IPs outside the Box View host's egress
Use of a non-expiring token long after the integration was retired
Both Primary and Secondary tokens in use at once (one may be leaked)

containment.steps: Regenerate/remove the Primary or Secondary App Token in Developer Console > Configuration; admin disables the app in Admin Console.
containment.notes: Box docs do not document revoking App Tokens or the effect of regeneration; verify in a test app.

sample_query.purpose: Review content access; filter created_by.login to the Limited Access App service account

unknown: App Token revoke/regenerate procedure and event
Whether POST /oauth2/revoke works on App Tokens

calls.reveals: the app's Service Account identity (App Token has access only to its own account)
calls.log_notes: Read event emission not documented; scope limited to app's own account

calls.reveals: items in the app's own account only
file contents in binary (within the app's own account)
